implementation_notes:
TASK-J004-020 has two coupled cleanup actions; both landed as small, surgical edits.

A. Phase 2 stub-anchor retirement gate.
  1. Cleaned three retirement-explanation docstrings in src/jarvis/tools/dispatch.py that still literally named the retired symbols (LOG_PREFIX_DISPATCH, _stub_response_hook, JARVIS_DISPATCH_STUB) — replaced with neutral descriptive text so a strict substring search finds zero matches in src/jarvis/. Removed the stale `DEGRADED: transport_stub` line from queue_build's docstring (queue_build's body never returned that string after TASK-J004-011's docstring rewrite; the line was orphaned).
  2. Extended tests/test_no_retired_roster_strings.py with class TestNoPhase2StubAnchors. The class is parametrised over four (forbidden_token, search_root) tuples: LOG_PREFIX_DISPATCH/_stub_response_hook/JARVIS_DISPATCH_STUB scoped to src/jarvis/, and `DEGRADED: transport_stub` scoped to src/jarvis/tools/. The DEGRADED-prefixed form for transport_stub respects DDR-009's stable error-vocabulary guarantee — bare `transport_stub` is preserved as a Literal entry on DispatchError per the design contract; only the full retired DEGRADED return-shape is asserted absent. The test failure message reports `<rel-path>:<line-no>` for every offending line so a future regression names the file + line as required by AC-002. Added a test_all_four_anchors_enumerated sanity guard so a typo in the parametrize fixture surfaces loudly.

B. test_routing_e2e.py update for the real-NATS path.
  1. Added imports for pytest_asyncio, MessageEnvelope, ResultPayload (no EventType — the subscriber replies with a bare ResultPayload because dispatch.py decodes the reply as ResultPayload directly, not as an envelope-wrapped payload).
  2. Added _build_routing_supervisor_with_nats helper mirroring the existing _build_routing_supervisor but passing nats_client through assemble_tool_list (attended) AND through the ambient_tool_factory closure (so DDR-014 Layer 3 sees the same handle).
  3. Added pytest_asyncio.fixture mocked_specialist_consumer that subscribes a wildcard handler on agents.command.> against the conftest in-process nats-server fixture and ack-replies success on every request. The reply is a real ResultPayload(success=True) JSON — no AsyncMock — so the dispatch tool's reply parser is exercised end-to-end. Teardown unsubscribes via contextlib.suppress so a half-drained connection cannot mask a test result.
  4. Added class TestRealNATSRoutingScenarios with two methods: (i) test_supervisor_routes_canned_prompt_via_nats parametrised over the same _SCENARIOS list as the original TestRoutingScenarios — same expected tool name, same first-call argument subset, same role-encoded JSON description for prompts 3-5 — proving the reasoning model's tool-call sequence is byte-identical across the transport swap; and (ii) test_dispatch_through_real_nats_returns_specialist_success which invokes dispatch_by_capability directly against the in-process broker + mocked specialist so the round-trip's success path is observable without depending on the canned LLM emitting a dispatch_by_capability tool call.
  5. Skip-clean when nats-server CLI is missing — the conftest fixture already handles that with a clear operator message (TASK-J004-014 floor capability), so the new class auto-skips without polluting the suite.

Lint/format/type: ruff (lint + format) clean on all three modified files; mypy strict on src/jarvis/tools/dispatch.py is clean. mypy on the two test files surfaces 13 pre-existing import-untyped + no-any-return errors that all exist on git HEAD without my changes (verified via `git stash && mypy ...`); none of my new code introduces a new mypy error.
